messages:
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@darklight.ai>

Cc: ops@darklight.ai, procurement@darklight.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency spike — queued requests and 502s

Soojin / David —

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors against our reserved capacity cluster starting ~07:50 PDT. Approx 18% of requests are queuing >2s and a handful of critical workflows are timing out. This is affecting our fraud detection pipeline (high priority for us right now).

We raised an incident internally but wanted Redwood on the thread ASAP because our metrics indicate our reserved throughput is being hit and requests are spilling to lower tiers with degraded model variants. Can you confirm whether this is a routing or pool saturation issue?

We're attaching a short sample of logs and span IDs. We also have procurement breathing down us for SLA credits if this escalates.

— Marta
Marta Gomez
Head of Engineering, DarkLight Analytics
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@darklight.ai>, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — queued requests and 502s

Marta — thanks for the heads up and for the log sample. We're triaging now. First pass from our incident board: reserved pool for DarkLight shows sustained CPU/GPU utilization at 98% across the pool starting 07:42, with elevated KV-cache misses. Initial thought: a temporary spike in long-context requests has pushed effective throughput above the reserved profile and continuous batching is growing queue depth.

Immediate next steps (short):
- David and infra on a hotfix path to forcibly evict stale KV prefixes and reduce cache pressure.
- Temporarily widen routing policy to allow BurstPool for 15 minutes (we'll limit model sizes to compatible variants).
- We'll stream metrics and proposed mitigation plan to your ops channel.

I'll schedule a 30-min bridge in 20 minutes and loop Marissa for exec alignment.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@darklight.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — queued requests and 502s

Quick technical update (attaching full trace bundle: darklight_spike_logs.zip). Observations from 07:30–08:15 window:
- Reserved GPU pool reached 98–100% SM utilization; host-level IO is nominal.
- We observed a sequence of long-sequence (>2048 tokens) requests from a single DarkLight job executor; those requests account for ~42% of tokens and inflated KV-cache churn.
- Continuous batching aggregated several of the long-context calls into a large micro-batch that exceeded our preferred kernel path, forcing a fallback kernel with ~2.3x latency.

Mitigation applied at 08:38:
1) Evicted KV prefixes heavier than 10k entries (reduces cache memory footprint).
2) Applied temporary model-variant restriction: long-context heavy requests routed to dedicated long-context backends (not shared reserved pool).
3) Enabled BurstPool for the next 20 minutes with token-level throttles.

Preliminary result: error rate dropped from 6.1% to 1.4% and p95 latency fell from 1.9s to 780ms. We'll keep monitoring. Priyom to follow up with a tuning recommendation for job-side batching limits.

— David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: DarkLight post-mitigation summary and next steps

Marta — quick post-mortem summary after 24h monitoring:
- Root cause: transient spike of long-context heavy jobs plus continuous-batching micro-batching that forced a fallback kernel path and pushed reserved pool to saturation.
- Impact: peak error rate 6.1%, average p95 latency increase to 1.9s for 30 minutes; approx 210k requests affected during the window.
- Immediate remediation executed: KV eviction, temporary model-variant segregation, BurstPool for 20–72 minutes (depending on contract amendment), and throttles on long sequences.

Action items (assigned):
- DarkLight engineering: apply client-side sequence-length cap + batching window cap (recommended values in the shared doc). Owner: Marta (ETA: 2027-04-05).
- Redwood SRE: implement persistent KV eviction policy for this reserved pool and add an alert for kernel-fallback rate >0.5%. Owner: David (ETA: 2027-04-04).
- Redwood Sales/Ops: finalize amendment and confirm 72-hour burst allocation if procurement signs. Owner: Marcus/Marissa (ETA: 2027-04-02 EOD).

We'll also schedule a 30-min postmortem with your CTO and our technical leadership next week. Thanks for the rapid coordination — please let us know if you need a formal credit timeline now or after the postmortem.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
